article.title: GM to Offer Hybrid Chevrolet Traverse, GMC Acadia, and Buick Enclave, According to Reuters

resolved.source_title: GM to Offer Hybrid Chevrolet Traverse, GMC Acadia, and Buick Enclave, According to Reuters

verification.title: GM to Offer Hybrid Chevrolet Traverse, GMC Acadia, and Buick Enclave, According to Reuters - MotorBiscuit

text:
After years of strictly pushing a fully electric future, General Motors is officially walking back its EV-only mandate and returning to gas-electric hybrids.
Following intense pressure from its own retail network, GM confirmed it will restructure a $500 million Department of Energy grant to prepare its Lansing Delta Township plant for future hybrid vehicle production. While GM declined to provide details on timing or specific models, a new report from Reuters states the Lansing facility will build hybrid versions of GM’s heavy-hitting three-row SUVs: the Chevrolet Traverse, Buick Enclave, and GMC Acadia.
The move represents a massive strategic pivot for an automaker that currently only sells one hybrid vehicle in the United States—the Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray.
GM Yielding to Dealer Pressure and Market Realities
The decision to hybridize GM’s largest crossovers is a direct response to shifting market demands. Over the first nine months of 2026, GM saw its U.S. market share drop to 16.6% from 17.4% a year earlier. Meanwhile, automakers that heavily invested in hybrid lineups, namely Toyota and Honda, gained ground.
This loss in market share sparked intense frustration among GM’s retail network.
“We’ve been telling them every chance we get that we need hybrids,” one dealer told Reuters, noting that retailers explicitly pressed GM sales executives for hybrid options during recent regional meetings.
GM executives previously dismissed hybrids as an unnecessary cost and complexity, preferring to funnel billions directly into battery-electric platforms. However, CEO Mary Barra officially confirmed the reversal during an earnings call last week.
“It’s not going to be additional [capital expenditures] and engineering. We’ll talk more about them as we get closer to the launch,” Barra confirmed as per Reuters.
The Current Three-Row Gas Lineup
Currently, GM’s three-row crossovers rely entirely on internal combustion engines, primarily utilizing turbocharged 2.5-liter four-cylinder powerplants. Adding a hybrid option would provide a much-needed boost to their fuel efficiency, which currently sits firmly in the middle of the pack.
For the 2025 model year, the current gas-powered models break down as follows:
- Chevrolet Traverse: Starts at $40,800. The standard front-wheel-drive (FWD) model achieves an EPA-estimated 23 MPG combined (20 city / 27 highway).
- GMC Acadia: Starts at $43,700. The FWD configuration yields an EPA-estimated 23 MPG combined (20 city / 27 highway).
- Buick Enclave: Starts at $45,200. The FWD version also returns an EPA-estimated 23 MPG combined (20 city / 27 highway).
Taking the Fight to Toyota
By electrifying the Traverse, Enclave, and Acadia, GM will finally give buyers a domestic alternative to the heavyweights of the three-row hybrid segment.
The most obvious targets are Toyota’s incredibly popular Highlander Hybrid and the larger Grand Highlander Hybrid, both of which have dominated the family-hauler hybrid space. A hybrid Traverse or Acadia will also have to contend with the Kia Sorento Hybrid (which currently achieves up to 36 MPG combined), the Hyundai Santa Fe Hybrid, and the plug-in hybrid (PHEV) variant of the Mazda CX-90.
While GM has not confirmed when these Lansing-built hybrids will hit dealership lots, the strategic pivot ensures that the automaker will not cede the lucrative family-hauler market to its electrified rivals.
